basics.name: Wenyang Liu
basics.label: Computer Vision, Multimodal AI & Content Understanding Researcher
basics.summary: Ph.D. researcher in computer vision and multimodal AI, building foundation-model-based systems for visual content understanding and real-world applications. First author of four CCF-A papers across CVPR, ACM MM, and IEEE TMM, with 21 publications, 340+ citations, and an h-index of 8. Experience spans few-/zero-shot learning, open-vocabulary perception, image and video restoration, and robotics.

work.name: Hyundai–NTU–A*STAR Corporate Lab, NTU
work.summary: Develop vision-based robotic perception systems for reliable industrial part picking in smart manufacturing.
highlights: Developed DriftAD, a visually-guided CLIP adaptation framework for few-shot anomaly detection, achieving up to 1.5-point gains in 1-shot AUROC and PRO (ACM MM 2026); extended the work to zero-shot detection with TRACE using CLIP and DINOv3
Built an open-vocabulary perception and grasping pipeline for unseen object categories, validated on industrial parts and demonstrated through on-site robotic grasping; filed a related patent

work.name: School of EEE, Nanyang Technological University
work.summary: Led research on image/video restoration, lightweight super-resolution, and corrupted multimedia recovery.
highlights: Developed a two-stage framework for bitstream-corrupted JPEG restoration reaching 38.92 dB PSNR on 2K images (+5.52 dB over EPDN); published as first author at CVPR 2023, extended through a collaborative NeurIPS 2023 study on corrupted-video recovery

Designed PromptSR, a 0.78M-parameter lightweight super-resolution model using cascade prompting, improving baselines by up to 0.48 dB (IEEE TMM 2026); extended to adaptive superpixel token aggregation in AsTaSR

Built Byte2Image and ByteNet to classify raw file fragments without extensions or metadata by fusing byte-sequence and visual representations, improving accuracy by up to 12.2% across two benchmarks (IEEE TMM 2024)

work.name: College of Computer Science, Chongqing University
work.summary: Researched energy-efficient video processing and machine learning acceleration.
highlights: Parallelized H.264 decoding at the task level with dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, improving decoding speed by 27-32% while reducing energy consumption by 23-25% across 720p-2160p video (ICPADS 2018)
Developed HolyLight, a nanophotonic accelerator for data-center CNN workloads achieving 13x higher throughput per watt than a ReRAM baseline, now cited 140+ times (DATE 2019)

courses: Thesis: From File Fragments to Images: Vision Image Restoration and Super-Resolution Using Deep Learning
Supervisors: Prof. Chau Lap-Pui (IEEE Fellow) and Assoc. Prof. Yap Kim-Hui
Efficient computing systems, low-power video decoding, AI hardware acceleration
